title: Site Induction
summary: Before anyone starts work, the employer must teach them how to recognize and avoid unsafe conditions and the rules that apply to their work. A good site induction covers those hazards, the chemicals on site, and who is allowed to run what.
talking_points: The employer must instruct each employee in the recognition and avoidance of unsafe conditions and in the regulations that apply to the work environment (29 CFR 1926.21(b)(2)).

Anyone who handles poisons, caustics or other harmful substances must be taught how to handle and use them safely, the hazards, the hygiene practices and the protective measures required (1926.21(b)(3)).
Anyone who handles flammable liquids, gases or toxic materials must be taught safe handling and use and made aware of the rules that apply (1926.21(b)(5)).
If harmful plants or animals are present on the site, exposed workers must be told about the hazards, how to prevent injury and the first aid to use (1926.21(b)(4)).
The employer must run a safety program that includes frequent and regular inspections of the job site, materials and equipment by competent persons (1926.20(b)(1)-(2)).
Only workers qualified by training or experience may operate equipment and machinery (1926.20(b)(4)).
Protections such as PPE and training are owed to each employee individually. Missing PPE or training for one worker is a separate failure (1926.20(f)).
Good practice: ask questions during the induction. If you do not know a hazard, a rule or who to call, say so before you start work.
site_hazards_to_check: New workers starting with no hazard orientation
Chemicals, flammable liquids or gases on site that a worker has not been trained to handle
Workers running equipment they are not qualified to operate
Required PPE not issued or not worn
No one named to carry out regular site inspections
Site-specific hazards (harmful plants or animals, restricted areas) not explained
discussion_questions: What hazards on this site would a brand-new person not know about?
What training must a worker have before handling flammable liquids or gases here?
Who does the regular inspections on this job, and how do we report a problem?
